draft.title: Similar figures and scale factor
card: Similar figures have the same shape but can be different sizes. Their matching angles are equal.
Matching sides are in the same ratio. Every side of one figure is the same number of times longer than the matching side of the other.
That number is the scale factor. Scale factor \(=\) new length \(\div\) original length.
Example: a rectangle 4 cm by 6 cm and a rectangle 12 cm by 18 cm. Each side is multiplied by \(12 \div 4 = 3\) and \(18 \div 6 = 3\), so the scale factor is 3.
draft.remember: Similar figures have equal angles, and every matching side is multiplied by the same scale factor.

a.q: A photo is 10 cm wide and 15 cm tall. An enlargement is 30 cm wide and 45 cm tall. What is the scale factor from the photo to the enlargement?
a.why: Scale factor \(=\) 30 \(\div\) 10 \(=\) 3, and 45 \(\div\) 15 \(=\) 3 as well. The option \(\frac{1}{3}\) comes from dividing the wrong way round: that would be the scale factor from the enlargement back to the photo.
a.clue: Divide a new length by the matching original length.

b.q: Rectangle A is 5 cm by 8 cm. Which rectangle is similar to A?
b.why: 10 cm by 16 cm has both sides multiplied by 2, so the sides are in the same ratio. For 10 cm by 13 cm, 5 is multiplied by 2 but 8 is not, so adding 5 to each side does not keep the shape.
b.clue: Check that both sides are multiplied by the same number.
